summary: Composio already runs a managed Gmail OAuth app, so you can connect users today without any Google setup. Your own app is only needed if you want your brand on the consent screen, your own scopes, or your own quota. Setting up your own Google Cloud OAuth client takes under an hour. The big gotcha is that almost every useful Gmail scope (mail.google.com, gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose) is "restricted". To let the public connect, you need Google's brand and scope verification plus a paid yearly CASA security assessment from a third party. That usually takes 2-6 weeks and vendor-reported costs of roughly $500-$4,500 a year.

verdict.difficultyReason: Dev setup is self-serve, but restricted Gmail scopes need Google verification plus a paid yearly third-party CASA security assessment before more than 100 outside users can connect.

devReady.estimate: 20-45 min (or 0 min using Composio's managed app)
devReady.detail: Create a Google Cloud project, enable the Gmail API, set Audience to External and leave it in Testing, add yourself as a test user, then create a Web OAuth client with Composio's redirect URI. You can then connect test accounts (100-user cap). In Testing mode, refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so connections break weekly. If your org has Google Workspace, an Internal app works for your org's users with no verification and no 7-day expiry.

productionReady.estimate: 2-6 weeks typical (reported); longer if the CASA scan finds issues
productionReady.detail: Publish the app (In production), complete brand verification (verified domain, homepage, privacy policy), and submit restricted-scope verification with a demo video and scope justifications. When Google's Trust & Safety team asks, complete a CASA security assessment with an approved assessor. Reported costs are about $540-$4,500 depending on assessor and tier. This must be redone every year. Until you are verified, users see an 'unverified app' warning and you are capped at 100 users. To skip all of this, use Composio's managed app (Composio branding, shared quota).

verdict.handsOnEffort: 1 hour for dev; 1-3 days total for production (policy pages, video, justifications, CASA scan fixes)

nextAction: Choose your path first. If Composio branding on the consent screen is acceptable, connect a test Gmail account through Composio's managed auth now and skip Google setup. If not, create a Google Cloud project and open Google Auth Platform at https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview.

accessPaths.name: Composio managed OAuth app
accessPaths.whenToUse: Prototypes, internal tools, and early launches where a 'Composio' consent screen is fine
accessPaths.limits: Consent screen shows Composio. Default scopes only. Quota is shared across all Composio customers. Triggers poll every 15 minutes at minimum.

accessPaths.name: Own app, Internal (Google Workspace org only)
accessPaths.whenToUse: Only users in your own Workspace / Cloud Identity org will connect
accessPaths.limits: Only accounts in your org can connect. No unverified warning and no 100-user cap. An org admin may need to allow the app.

accessPaths.name: Own app, External in Testing / unverified
accessPaths.whenToUse: Development, staging, demos to a handful of named users
accessPaths.limits: Only listed test users can connect, 100 at most. Users see the 'Google hasn't verified this app' screen. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days for non-basic scopes.

accessPaths.name: Own app, External, verified for restricted scopes
accessPaths.whenToUse: Public product where any Gmail user can connect under your brand
accessPaths.timeline: 2-6 weeks typical, then a yearly re-assessment
accessPaths.limits: No user cap once verified. Gmail API per-user and per-project quotas apply. CASA is required every year.

prerequisites.item: Google account and Google Cloud project
prerequisites.detail: Any Google account can create a project. Use separate projects for dev and prod, because Google exempts dev/staging projects from verification.

prerequisites.item: Domain you own, verified in Google Search Console
prerequisites.detail: Every authorized domain on the consent screen must be verified by a project Owner or Editor through Search Console. You need this for production only.

prerequisites.item: Public homepage and privacy policy on that domain
prerequisites.detail: The homepage must describe the app and can't be only a login page. The privacy policy must be on the same domain, linked from the homepage, and must explain how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared. It should also include the Limited Use disclosure. Needed for production.
Shows the full OAuth flow with the English consent screen and the exact scopes, then each feature that uses each scope. Needed for sensitive or restricted scope verification.

A third-party assessor (for example TAC Security) charges roughly $540-$4,500 per year (vendor prices reported by integration platforms; Google's Security Assessment page publishes no fee). Needed for restricted scopes in production.
Shown on the consent screen. Uploading a logo triggers brand verification.

phases.title: Register the app in Google Cloud
phases.goal: A Google Cloud project with the Gmail API enabled and a Web OAuth client ID and secret

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Go to the Cloud Console, open the project picker, then New Project. Name it something like [APP]-gmail-dev. Make a separate prod project later.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Open APIs & Services > Library, search for 'Gmail API', and click Enable. If you keep Composio's default People scopes (contacts, birthday, addresses), enable the People API as well.

steps.title: Configure Branding and Audience
steps.detail: Open Google Auth Platform > Branding and set the app name, support email, developer contact, and (later) logo, homepage, privacy policy and authorized domain. Under Audience, choose Internal if only your Workspace org will connect. Otherwise choose External and leave the status as Testing. Under Test users, add your own Gmail addresses (100 at most).

steps.title: Add scopes under Data Access
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Data Access > Add or remove scopes. Add only what your agent needs. Examples: gmail.send (sensitive) or gmail.readonly / gmail.modify (restricted). https://mail.google.com/ gives full access and is restricted.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Clients > Create client. Set Application type to Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs, add exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret, because the secret may only be fully shown once.

phases.title: Connect through Composio and test
phases.goal: Your own Gmail account connects through your custom auth config and the agent can call Gmail tools

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, go to Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Gmail > OAuth2. Paste your Client ID and Client Secret and set your scopes. Confirm that the redirect URI shown matches the one you registered. Click Create and copy the ac_... ID.

steps.title: Pass the auth config in your session
steps.detail: Set authConfigs: { gmail: 'ac_...' } in the Composio session. Toolkits you don't list keep using managed auth.

steps.title: Run a test connection
steps.detail: Connect with a test-user account. Click through 'Google hasn't verified this app' (Advanced > Go to [APP]). Then call a read tool such as listing messages. In Testing mode, expect invalid_grant after 7 days and reconnect.

phases.title: Verify for production (restricted scopes)
phases.goal: App is In production and verified, so any Gmail user can connect without a warning or the 100-user cap
phases.waitTime: Reported 2-6 weeks total. Google's review plus CASA, where CASA is usually the longer part.

steps.title: Publish homepage and privacy policy on a verified domain
steps.detail: Verify the domain in Google Search Console with a project Owner/Editor account. Put the privacy policy on the same domain and link it from the homepage. Include Google API Services User Data Policy / Limited Use language.

steps.title: Narrow scopes and write justifications
steps.detail: Google rejects broad scopes that a narrower scope could replace. For example, don't request mail.google.com if gmail.modify is enough. Remove Composio's default People/contacts scopes unless you use them, since they add more sensitive scopes to the review. Use the drafts below.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Set the consent screen language to English. Show the full sign-in and consent screen with the exact scopes listed, then show each feature that uses each scope. If data is used for AI training, show explicit user consent. Upload to YouTube as unlisted.

steps.title: Publish and submit for verification
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Audience > Publish app. Then go to Verification Center and submit. Reply quickly to Trust & Safety emails, because slow replies stall the review.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: When Google's Trust & Safety team asks, pick an approved assessor (TAC Security is the commonly reported discounted one). Run the scan, fix findings (often TLS/header config), and get the Letter of Validation. Self-scanning first with OWASP ZAP helps.

phases.title: Ongoing maintenance
phases.goal: Connections keep working and verification stays valid
phases.duration: A few hours a year plus CASA renewal

steps.title: Renew CASA every year
steps.detail: Google requires restricted-scope apps to be revalidated every year. Reported to be easier than the first time, but it is paid.

steps.title: Handle refresh-token loss
steps.detail: Tokens die if unused for 6 months, if the user changes their password (Gmail scopes), if the user revokes access, or if there are more than 100 tokens per account per client (the oldest is dropped silently). Prompt users to reconnect on invalid_grant.

steps.title: Re-verify when scopes change
steps.detail: Adding a new sensitive or restricted scope requires another verification submission.

scopes.purpose: Full Gmail access, including permanent delete, IMAP/SMTP (Composio default)
scopes.reviewNote: Restricted: verification + CASA. Google pushes back hard if a narrower scope would do.

scopes.purpose: Read, compose, send, label and trash mail (no permanent delete)
scopes.reviewNote: Restricted: verification + CASA. Usually the right choice for a full agent.
Sensitive: verification with a demo video, but no CASA. Use it alone if the agent only sends.
Believed non-sensitive; confirm in the Data Access panel
Sensitive: adds to verification scope. Drop it if you don't use it.

blockers.title: Unverified app warning / 100-user cap
blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app'. New users are blocked once 100 users have connected.
blockers.fix: Use Testing with named test users for dev, choose an Internal audience for Workspace-only use, or complete verification. You can also fall back to Composio's managed app.

blockers.title: Connections die after 7 days
blockers.symptom: invalid_grant on refresh about a week after connecting
blockers.fix: This is expected for External apps in Testing status with Gmail scopes. Publish the app to In production (and verify), or use an Internal audience.

blockers.title: Access blocked: user not a test user
blockers.symptom: Error 403: access_denied, 'app is currently being tested'
blockers.fix: Add the account under Google Auth Platform > Audience > Test users.

blockers.title: redirect_uri_mismatch
blockers.symptom: Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch on the Google consent page
blockers.fix: Add exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add to the Web client's Authorized redirect URIs. Exact match is required, including the trailing path.

blockers.title: Verification rejected for overly broad scopes or a weak video
blockers.symptom: Trust & Safety email asking you to narrow scopes or re-record the demo
blockers.fix: Swap mail.google.com for gmail.modify/readonly/send where possible. Show every scope in use in the video, with the consent screen in English.

blockers.title: CASA scan findings
blockers.symptom: Assessor reports vulnerabilities (TLS config, headers) and validation stalls
blockers.fix: Pre-scan with OWASP ZAP, fix findings, and use the included revalidations. Follow up daily with the assessor and Google.

blockers.title: Workspace admin blocks the app
blockers.symptom: admin_policy_enforced or 'access blocked by your administrator'
blockers.fix: The customer's Workspace admin must trust the app's client ID in Admin console > Security > API controls.

blockers.title: Users grant only some scopes (granular consent)
blockers.symptom: A connected account works for reading but tool calls that send or modify mail fail with insufficient permission errors.
blockers.fix: Since January 2026 Google shows each scope as a separate checkbox. Check the granted scopes returned with the token, explain in your UI why each one is needed, and re-prompt for missing scopes instead of assuming all were granted.

technical.pkce: Supported (S256 and plain, per discovery). Optional for confidential web clients.
technical.refreshTokens: Access tokens last about 1 hour. Refresh tokens are issued only with access_type=offline, and reliably only on first consent or with prompt=consent. They expire after 7 days for External apps in Testing. They are revoked after 6 months unused, on password change (Gmail scopes), on user revocation, on admin policy, or when there are more than 100 tokens per account per client ID (the oldest is invalidated). Google also caps refresh tokens at 100 per Google Account per OAuth client ID; issuing a 101st silently invalidates the oldest, so avoid re-running consent unnecessarily.
technical.redirectUriRules: Exact match against the Web client's Authorized redirect URIs. HTTPS is required except localhost. No wildcards. Register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.
technical.notes: OIDC discovery is at accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration. No tenant-specific URLs. Gmail API quota is per project, so your own app avoids Composio's shared quota. Real-time triggers can use Gmail push via Pub/Sub; Composio managed polls at 15+ minutes. Internal audience requires an org-owned project.

Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console

drafts.title: Restricted scope justification (gmail.modify)
drafts.purpose: Google Auth Platform > Data Access / Verification Center scope justification field
drafts.content: [APP NAME] is an AI assistant that helps users manage their own Gmail inbox. We request https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify so the assistant can, only when the user asks: (1) read and summarize messages and threads the user selects or searches for, (2) draft and send replies on the user's behalf after the user confirms, and (3) apply labels, archive, and mark messages read. gmail.readonly is insufficient because the user-requested actions of sending replies and labeling/archiving require write access; gmail.send alone cannot read the thread being replied to. We do not need permanent deletion, so we do not request https://mail.google.com/. Gmail data is used only to provide these user-facing features, is not used for advertising, is not sold or transferred, and [is / is not] used to train generalized AI models. Data is stored [for X days / not stored beyond the request], encrypted at rest. Privacy policy: [PRIVACY URL].

drafts.title: Demo video script
drafts.purpose: Recording the YouTube demo for verification
drafts.content: 1. Show [APP URL] homepage with app name matching the consent screen. 2. Click 'Connect Gmail'. Show the browser URL bar containing client_id=[CLIENT ID]. 3. Show the full Google consent screen in English, pausing on the list of scopes: [LIST SCOPES]. 4. Grant access. 5. Ask the agent: 'Summarize my unread emails from today' and show the result (gmail.modify read). 6. Ask: 'Reply to [SENDER] saying [TEXT]', then show the confirmation and the sent message in Gmail (send). 7. Ask: 'Label this as [LABEL] and archive it', then show the result in Gmail (modify). 8. Show how the user disconnects / revokes access in [SETTINGS PAGE].

drafts.title: Reviewer test instructions
drafts.content: Test account for [APP NAME]: [TEST LOGIN EMAIL] / [PASSWORD] (no 2FA). Steps: sign in at [APP URL], go to Settings > Integrations > Connect Gmail and complete Google consent with any Gmail account. Then in the chat box type 'Summarize my last 5 emails' (read), 'Draft a reply to the latest email saying thanks' and confirm (send), 'Archive that email' (modify). Contact [SUPPORT EMAIL] for any issue.

Probe: authorize endpoint with unregistered client

probes.observed: 200. authorization_endpoint https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token_endpoint https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, PKCE plain+S256, grants authorization_code/refresh_token/device_code/jwt-bearer, no registration_endpoint.
probes.conclusion: Endpoints confirmed and PKCE is supported. No dynamic client registration, so you must create the client in Cloud Console.

probes.action: Authorize request with an unregistered client_id, Composio redirect URI, scope https://mail.google.com/, access_type=offline
probes.observed: 302 to accounts.google.com/signin/oauth/error with authError decoding to 'invalid_client: The OAuth client was not found.' (error 401)
probes.conclusion: The endpoint is live. Google checks the client before the redirect URI. A wrong or typo'd client ID shows 'Error 401: invalid_client'.

probes.observed: 302 to the Google sign-in page (ServiceLogin, service=cloudconsole)
probes.conclusion: The console URL exists and requires a Google login.

probes.observed: OAUTH2. Composio provides a managed app. Redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Default scopes include mail.google.com plus People API profile/contacts scopes.
probes.conclusion: No Google setup is needed to start. Your own app is optional for branding, scopes and quota.

uncertainties: Exact Google review timelines are not published. The 2-6 week range comes from developer and vendor reports and depends on how fast you respond.
CASA cost and tier (AL1 vs AL2) vary by assessor and app. The figures are from 2025-2026 community posts and may have changed.
Exact menu labels in the new Google Auth Platform UI (Branding, Audience, Clients, Data Access, Verification Center) were not seen while logged in.
Whether gmail.labels is still classed as non-sensitive was not checked against the live Data Access panel.
Whether Composio's managed Gmail app remains verified for all its default scopes, and its per-user quota share, were not checked.
